questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the culture and location was not too far from Denmark. The language and culture. I wanted to learn more of the language and I already had some friends from the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great. I developed a lot as a person and had an amazing experience meeting so many nice people and experiencing the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I asked some students for directions. There was a mail to write to in case we had trouble with something. The people in the university office were really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We had an exchange introduction week which was very nice. There we met a lot of the other exchange students and got an introduction to the Netherlands, the associations at the school and the country in general. It was a bit confusing, like insider knowledge when we didn’t know anything already, but it gave us an overview. The introduction week was really important in the later social life.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student housing. A big room and shared bathroom and kitchen. I had my own kitchen and shared with one person. There were two different student accommodation buildings on campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had our own or shared kitchen. There was also a food court with different stores on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Hatta is great. It's really nice to live on campus. There is a swap shop where you can get things for free. They don't allow us to leave any things there, but in the end of the semester there is a whole pile of people's stuff in the basement free to take. So with a bit of planning or coming a bit before you can get all things for free. 
It's not really clean and the beds are very hard. Some people buy a mattress topper. But otherwise the rooms are very fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to enroll for courses online at a specific date.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an email but nothing they could really do about the system of registration that I was too late for the course I wanted or had two exams at the same time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was a bit late in the first round so I didn’t get one of the classes I wanted. I got two others that I wanted, but the problem was the schedule. Many classes were at the same time but I just had to check that when choosing. It was hard to find information about the schedule of the exams so I ended up having two exams at the same time. I managed to complete both within the 3 hours though. Second term (second half of the semester) I knew this so it was better.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the exam and course schedules. Some courses don’t have physical exams but just an essay to write. And register exactly at the time they open the registrations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very. It’s a very good university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of them were quite hard and challenging which if found very nice. I learned a lot from it. Others were first year courses on the bachelor so very introductory and easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: For most classes they talked about the texts which was nice. The teachers were mostly very engaged and interesting. I like the way they teach with passion.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology, Culture and Modernity
Social Media Marketing
The Future of the Cultural and Creative Sector
Management of the Cultural and Creative Industries
Feeling Orange - Perspectives on Dutch Culture
Organizations and Communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sociology, Culture and Modernity! It was very good and I learned a lot from it. Very interesting sociological critiques of modern society rooted in the 19th century thinkers. Still very relevant today. The teacher was good and explained the texts that could be hard. On their website it says that the course is heavy and hard, but if you’re there for class, understand and study to remember what you learn, it is very rewarding. 
Feeling Orange was fun and mandatory. We learned about different aspects of the Dutch culture and had to write an essay to compare an aspect to a case in our own countries. It was a fast general overview but made us understand a bit better.

questions.answer: Alcohol is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a bar, a food court, a sports building where you can get a sports pass for 159 euros for 6 months and have unlimited access to a gym and all different sports classes (zumba, yoga, kickboxing …) and tennis-, badminton- and squash courts.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
There are different associations on campus. I joined the music association. Do it early. It’s a good way to meet locals too and find people with the same interests. 
The sports pass also.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go visit other cities like Den Haag, Amsterdam, Utrecht, Delft, Gouda. 
Go to the Kralingen Lake and around that area. Or Nesselande Beach. Or the beach in the Hague.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Pretty easy. The traffic is more chaotic. Trams don't go at night after 1. 
Language was fine. I understood. The culture is not that different, I think.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join an association of your interest.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They sing a lot in Dutch. Otherwise fine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The biking and the amount of celebrations for different events like king’s day, liberation day festival the 5th of may and local festivals. Friendly people working in public sector.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Many, if not all, exams are closed book, meaning that you can’t bring any notes. You have to study to understand and remember the content which is different than at UCPH. They have either essay questions where you have to write 100-300 words on each question and around 10 questions or multiple choice exams. The multiple choice exams I took were quite easy. 
The grading system is 1-10 with decimals where you need 5.5 to pass. But for most people the grades are just transferred as passed or failed. If you fail the first exam you have a second chance. Most courses have an activity like a presentation or an essay that count for certain amount of the final grade.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and all the random and fun activities we did.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my boyfriend.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
